Alright, let me think through this year on my land.

---

I've been working this ground for 30 years — I know what it gives me. Of my 31.5 mu, I keep 28 mu in the wheat-maize rotation like most folks around here, and 3.5 mu near the road for zucchini where the well is close and I can haul to market easy. With only my wife and me really working the land (our kid works in town), I can't do too much zucchini even though it pays better — it needs picking every other day once it starts.

**Wheat** went in last October, so right now I'm thinking about topdressing. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, about one bag of 15-15-15 per mu plus some urea, maybe 20 kg N per mu total once I topdress at green-up and jointing. The extension guy keeps saying 15 is enough but my land's been farmed hard and I'd rather spend the extra 30 yuan than watch it go yellow. I'll water it at jointing and again at grain fill — twice if the spring rain comes, three times if it's dry. Hoping for 450 kg/mu, same as last year.

**Maize** goes right in after wheat harvest in June — tight turnaround, maybe 5 days. I use no-till direct seeding with a hybrid seed (Zhengdan or similar, whatever the shop has), about 80 yuan/mu for seed. Base fertilizer at planting, urea topdress at big trumpet stage, around 16 kg N/mu total. One irrigation if the summer rain is good, two if it's dry. Maize is less fussy than wheat. I expect about 500 kg/mu.

**Zucchini** is the cash crop. It takes more work and more inputs — I plow it properly, use plastic mulch, drip line from the well. Puts in about 25 kg N/mu across the season, plus manure I get cheap from the pig farmer down the road. Costs more but I can clear 2000-3000 yuan per mu if the market holds. My wife handles most of the picking and the vegetable buyer comes through twice a week.

Total input cash this year will run me maybe 14,000 yuan. Tight but manageable. If fertilizer prices jumped again I'd cut the maize rate first — wheat and zucchini I won't skimp on.
